Subject: Novaplay — inference interop checklist & side-by-side tests

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: validate parity vs current hyperscaler for streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured output enforcement for Novaplay’s recommendation pipeline.
- Key success criteria you mentioned: token-level streaming latency, stable tool-invocation reliability, and deterministic JSON output for downstream ingestion.

Proposed small side-by-side (SxS) test scope (30–90m):
1) Streaming probe — 1k sample prompts representative of your UX flows; measure token p95/p99 latency and partial-output arrival behavior.
2) Function-calling / tool invocation — run 200 simulated tool calls (external webhooks) across model variants to measure end-to-end success and failure modes.
3) Structured output conformance — validate output against your JSON schema, measure conformance and common deviation patterns.

Deliverables we’ll bring: test matrix, runnable test scripts, and per-route latency/cost summary. Marissa (cc’d) will lead engineering runs; Karthik will own model/config mapping.

Immediate asks for you (quick returns):
- Send the short requirements list (schema + sample prompts) — you can reply to this thread (PDF or Drive link).
- Confirm whether we should include Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B endpoints in the SxS.

Attachments: Novaplay_requirements_v1.pdf (requested during the call)

I’ll follow up with a concrete SxS calendar and a test matrix tomorrow.

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Thanks Logan — attaching the requirements PDF (Novaplay_requirements_v1.pdf). A few clarifications from our side before we lock the SxS slot: 

1) Streaming SLA: can you confirm token-streaming latency targets you typically hit in production (p95 token latency)? Hyperscaler A is currently at ~180ms p95 for our median prompt length; we’re curious where Redwood lands with similar configs.

2) Function calling: our toolflow requires an external HTTP callback (order creation simulation + DB write). Can you emulate end-to-end invocation (we’ll provide a sandbox callback endpoint)? We want to see retries/backoff and error surface.

3) Structured outputs: we need guaranteed schema conformance for the 3 most common response types (product_reco, price_adjust, attribution). How does Redwood detect and surface schema drift?

4) Pricing: can you share the quick pricing sheet for the SxS run and estimated per-token unit costs if we move to Redwood dedicated?

If that looks good we can do the SxS run early next week.

— Marta
Senior Product Manager, Novaplay
marta.silva@novaplay.com

Marta — great questions, answered inline and a proposed test matrix below. Attached: novaplay-sxs-test-matrix.xlsx and our quick pricing sheet (redwood-quick-pricing-sheet.csv).

Streaming SLA
- Typical production: p95 token-level latency in the 120–160ms range for configurations matching your median prompt length (single-stream, batch size tuned for latency). For SxS we’ll run with identical sequence-length distribution and report p50/p90/p95/p99.

Function calling (end-to-end)
- Yes, we can run against your sandbox callback. Test will include: successful calls, simulated 500s/timeouts, and flaky responses to exercise retries. We’ll capture end-to-end latency plus per-call success rate.

Structured outputs
- Test plan: run 500 validation checks per response type against your JSON schema. We’ll report conformance rate and example failure classes. For continuous monitoring we can add a schema-enforcement layer (auto-reject or auto-repair heuristics) depending on your preference.

Proposed pass thresholds for the SxS (editable):
- Streaming: p95 token latency <= 160ms; p99 <= 300ms
- Function-calling: end-to-end success rate >= 98% with <1% silent failures
- Schema conformance: >= 99% for target types

SxS logistics
- Owners: Marissa (engineering lead) / Karthik (model/config).
- Hyperscalers to include: Hyperscaler A (your current), Hyperscaler B (optional) — confirm which endpoints and API keys you want us to hit.
- Timeline: propose Tue 2026-08-03 for the technical run (1–2 hours).

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/3425
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleDriveLink

Next ask from you: confirm sandbox callback URL and which hyperscaler endpoints to include. If Novaplay can provide API keys by EOD Monday we’ll schedule the run.

Thanks — I’ll book a short 30m alignment with Marissa and Karthik after you confirm.

Best,
Logan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Forwarding Novaplay thread — they confirmed they want Hyperscaler A included and can provide sandbox callback Monday. Action items for engineering: 

- Run the SxS matrix attached (novaplay-sxs-test-matrix.xlsx). Primary targets: streaming probe, function-calling E2E, and schema conformance.
- Test owners: Marissa (streaming + metrics capture), Karthik (model variants + config mapping).
- Environment: mirror Novaplay median prompt lengths, run 1k streaming samples, 200 function-calls, 500 schema validations.
- Metrics to capture: token p50/p90/p95/p99, partial-output arrival times, end-to-end function success rate, and JSON schema conformance rate. Include per-token cost estimate for each run.
- Logging: capture raw streaming traces (timestamps per partial chunk) and attach to Drive folder.

Timeline: can we have an internal dry run by Mon 2026-08-02 so we’re green for the customer technical run on Tue 2026-08-03?

Notes: they want clear pass/fail thresholds (see my email above). If we see systematic schema drift we should prepare a short playbook with quick mitigations (prompt engineering + model fallback).

— Logan
